ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Tā Moko: A Record of an Individual's Path

fullPassage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice of the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual's journey from their past to their present. Each curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person's whakapapa (genealogy), social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire faces, while women have it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of passage throughout their lives. Although tā moko is less common these days, it is still practiced today by Maori people, who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage for the next generation.

questions.passage: Tā ①<u>moko</u> is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, <u>which</u> has been a culturally significant practice of the Maori for thousands of years. It is not ②<u>only</u> decorative but also <u>symbolic</u> of an individual's journey from their past to their present. ③<u>Each</u> curved line and pattern of tā moko <u>represent</u> a person's whakapapa, social positions, and personal accomplishments. ④<u>This</u> explains why no two tā moko designs <u>look</u> the same.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 타 모코의 각각의 곡선과 패턴은 한 사람의 족보를 나타낸다(represents).
det.analysis: ✅ ③ represent → represents: 주어가 'Each curved line and pattern'으로 each가 이끄는 단수 주어. 단수동사 represents 필요. ❌ ① which: 선행사 tattooing을 수식하는 계속적 관계대명사 적절. ❌ ② symbolic: 'not only A but also B' 병렬에서 형용사 적절. ❌ ④ look: 'no two designs'는 복수 주어이므로 복수동사 적절.
det.tip: each + 단수명사 + 단수동사: Each line represents ~. no two + 복수명사 + 복수동사.

questions.passage: Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head ①<u>to be</u> the most sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces. Men ②<u>typically</u> wear tā moko over their entire faces, while women have it on their lips and chins. The Maori start ③<u>to get</u> these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are ④<u>adding</u> to their tattoos to reflect their life experiences.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 더 많은 선과 모양이 문신에 추가된다(added).
det.analysis: ✅ ④ adding → added: 'lines and shapes are added'에서 수동태(be + p.p.) 필요. 선과 모양이 '추가되는' 것이지 스스로 '추가하는' 것이 아님. ❌ ① to be: 'consider + O + to be C(~를 C로 여기다)' 적절. ❌ ② typically: 부사로 동사 wear 수식 적절. ❌ ③ to get: 'start to V / start V-ing' 둘 다 가능.
det.tip: 수동태: be + p.p. are added(추가되다). consider + O + to be + C: ~를 C로 여기다.

questions.passage: Tā ①<u>moko</u> is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally <u>significant</u> practice. It is not ②<u>only</u> <u>decorating</u> but also symbolic of an individual's journey. ③<u>Each</u> curved line represents a person's whakapapa and personal accomplishments. ④<u>Although</u> tā moko is less common these days, it is still <u>practiced</u> today by Maori people, <u>who</u> hope to preserve their traditions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 장식적(decorative)일 뿐만 아니라 상징적이기도 하다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② decorating → decorative: 'not only A but also B'에서 B가 형용사(symbolic)이므로 A도 형용사 필요. decorating(현재분사/동명사)이 아닌 decorative(형용사). ❌ ① significant: 형용사로 practice 수식 적절. ❌ ③ practiced: 수동태 'is practiced by' 적절. ❌ ④ who: 선행사 Maori people을 수식하는 관계대명사 적절.
det.tip: not only A but also B: A와 B는 같은 품사. decorative(형용사) ↔ decorating(분사). symbolic(형용사)과 병렬.

questions.passage: ①<u>Each</u> curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person's whakapapa, social positions, and personal accomplishments. ②<u>This</u> explains <u>why</u> no two tā moko designs look the same. ③<u>Traditionally</u>, the Maori have <u>considered</u> the head to be the most sacred part of the body. Men ④<u>typically</u> wear tā moko over their entire faces, <u>while</u> women have it on their lips and chins. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of passage <u>among</u> their lives.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 문신은 삶의 전반에 걸쳐(throughout) 통과 의례로서 큰 중요성을 지녔다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④ among → throughout: 원문은 'throughout their lives(삶 전반에 걸쳐)'. among(~사이에서)은 여러 대상 사이를 의미하며, 삶의 전반을 뜻하는 throughout가 적절. ❌ ① why: 'explains why ~(왜 ~인지 설명하다)' 간접의문문 적절. ❌ ② considered: 현재완료 'have considered' 적절. ❌ ③ while: 대조의 접속사 '반면에' 적절.
det.tip: throughout(~전반에 걸쳐) ≠ among(~사이에서). throughout their lives = 일생에 걸쳐.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 각 곡선은 족보, 사회적 지위, 개인적 업적을 나타낸다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④accomplishments(업적): 원문 그대로. 족보, 사회적 지위와 함께 긍정적 기록을 나타냄. ❌ ①obstacles(장애물): 문신에 장애물을 새기는 것은 부자연스러움. ❌ ②regrets(후회): 긍정적 기록 맥락과 불일치. ❌ ③traditions(전통): 개인적 전통은 어색함.
det.tip: accomplishment: 업적, 성취 (= achievement). personal accomplishments = 개인적 업적.

questions.passage: The ①<u>Maori</u> start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect their life experiences. ②<u>Tattooing</u> traditionally held great importance as a rite of passage throughout their lives. ③<u>Although</u> tā moko is less <u>common</u> these days, it is still practiced today by Maori people, who hope to <u>preserve</u> their traditions and heritage for the next <u>generation</u>. ④<u>Each</u> design is <u>identical</u>, reflecting the unique path of each individual.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 각 디자인은 고유하다(unique). identical(동일한)은 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ④identical(동일한): 원문은 'no two tā moko designs look the same', 즉 모든 디자인이 고유(unique)함. identical은 정반대. ❌ ①common(흔한): 원문 그대로. ❌ ②preserve(보존하다): 원문 그대로. ❌ ③generation(세대): 원문 그대로.
det.tip: identical(동일한) ↔ unique(고유한). no two ~ look the same = 모두 다르다.

det.tip: 오류찾기에서 주어/목적어 뒤바꿈은 빈출 함정. head(머리) ↔ body(몸) 위치 주의.

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice of the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual's journey from their past to their present. Each curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person's whakapapa (genealogy), social positions, and personal __________. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire faces, while women have it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of passage throughout their lives.

det.korean: 개인적 업적(accomplishments)을 나타낸다.
det.analysis: 원문 'personal accomplishments'에서 직접 찾을 수 있다. 족보(whakapapa), 사회적 지위(social positions)와 함께 병렬.
det.tip: accomplishment: 업적, 성취 (= achievement). personal accomplishments = 개인적 업적.

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice of the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual's journey from their past to their present. Each curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person's whakapapa (genealogy), social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire faces, while women have it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of passage throughout their lives. Although tā moko is less common these days, it is still practiced today by Maori people, who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage for the next generation.

det.korean: 타 모코가 개인의 족보, 지위, 업적을 반영하는 문화적으로 중요한 관행임을 설명하는 글.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 타 모코가 개인의 여정/족보/업적을 상징한다는 것이 글의 핵심. ❌ ①: 다양한 예술이 아닌 타 모코 하나에 집중. ❌ ③: 현대 유행이 아닌 전통 문화. ❌ ④: 종교 의식이 아닌 문화적 관행.
det.tip: 주제 찾기: 반복 키워드(represents, symbolic, journey, accomplishments)에 주목.

questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Tā moko, a traditional Maori tattoo art, functions as a __(A)__ record of each individual's life, and despite becoming less __(B)__, it is still practiced to preserve cultural heritage.

det.korean: 타 모코는 개인 삶의 상징적(symbolic) 기록이며, 덜 흔해(common)졌지만 여전히 행해진다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①: (A) symbolic: 원문 'symbolic of an individual's journey'. (B) common: 원문 'less common these days'. ❌ ②: written(문서 기록)이 아닌 symbolic(상징적 기록). ❌ ③: valuable(가치 있는)은 less와 어울리지만 원문은 common. ❌ ④: historical(역사적)보다 symbolic이 더 정확.
det.tip: 요약 문제: 핵심 키워드(symbolic, common) 찾기. 원문 반복 단어가 정답 단서.

det.korean: 타 모코는 오늘날에도 여전히 마오리족에 의해 행해진다(practiced).
det.analysis: practice(동사원형) → practiced(과거분사). 'is still practiced by'에서 수동태(be + p.p.)가 필요.
det.tip: 수동태: be + p.p. is practiced(행해지다). practice: 행하다. practised = British spelling도 인정.
